overview.en: It is one of five Ictiobus sucker species. It can hybridize with Smallmouth Buffalo, Ictiobus bubalus.
overview.fr: C’est l’une des cinq espèces de meuniers Ictiobus. Il peut s’hybrider avec le Buffalo à petite bouche, Ictiobus bubalus.

identification.en: It reaches 91 cm and 36 kg; its large mouth lacks barbels.
identification.fr: Il atteint 91 cm et 36 kg; sa grande bouche n’a pas de barbillons.

habitat.en: It favors slow rivers, lakes and reservoirs.
habitat.fr: Il préfère les rivières lentes, les lacs et les réservoirs.

behavior.en: Spring floods prompt movement toward spawning grounds.
behavior.fr: Les crues printanières entraînent des déplacements vers les frayères.

reproduction.en: It spawns in spring and scatters eggs over vegetation.
reproduction.fr: Il fraie au printemps et disperse ses œufs sur la végétation.

ecology.en: Unlike many suckers, it eats plankton as well as benthos.
ecology.fr: Contrairement à beaucoup de meuniers, il mange du plancton et des organismes benthiques.

conservation.en: In 2008, Canadian populations received different regional status designations.
conservation.fr: En 2008, les populations canadiennes ont reçu des statuts régionaux différents.

title.en: Bigmouth Buffalo — USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species Database
title.fr: Buffalo à grande bouche — base des espèces aquatiques non indigènes de l’USGS

facts: USGS reports hybridization with Smallmouth Buffalo, spring spawning with eggs attached to vegetation, and feeding on plankton as well as benthos.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

title.en: Bigmouth Buffalo — COSEWIC status assessment and update report
title.fr: Buffalo à grande bouche — évaluation et rapport de situation du COSEPAC

facts: Report summarizes taxonomy, size, filtering diet, slow-water habitat, spring movements and Canadian population statuses.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

uncertainties: The conservation sentence summarizes the 2009 Canadian assessment only; its population-level designations are historical and geographically limited.
review_note: Compared USGS species ecology with the French COSEPAC report; kept the older Canadian statuses explicitly regional and dated, and noted the documented hybrid relative.
